Shenzhen深圳

The fastest registration in the country, and the shortest path from prototype to factory.

Registered address
¥6k–22k / year
Typical setup
2–5 weeks
Region
Greater Bay Area
Best suited to
Hardware, software,跨境 e-commerce, supply-chain technology and any founder who wants to be within an hour of the factory that makes their product.

Shenzhen is the city where the paperwork moves. Registration can complete in days, the district service centres are used to foreign applicants, and the supplier ecosystem for electronics, hardware and e-commerce is unmatched. It is also the most competitive market for engineers and the least forgiving on intellectual property.

The city's foreign-founder community is smaller than Shanghai's but more product-focused. Qianhai, the free-trade zone in the west, is the usual home for structures that need cross-border capital or Hong Kong proximity.

What actually differs here?

Shenzhen is the best city in China to build a physical product and the worst to be vague about ownership. Get the IP assignment in writing before the tooling is cut.

Address supply is abundant and cheap in Bao'an and Longgang; Nanshan and Futian cost more but signal credibility to investors and banks.

Before you commit to an address here

The figures on this page are ranges. District practice decides whether a specific address will register, bank and pass inspection — and it changes without much notice.

Take it to the counter: ask the district market regulator and the bank to confirm the address before you sign the lease, using the script in how to verify.

How to check it

Registration practice

How the paperwork actually goes in Shenzhen

Registry speed, address rules and the district-level differences that decide whether a plan is realistic.

Registering

Registration is online through the municipal portal with district review, and most districts offer a one-stop window for the business licence, seals and tax registration. Qianhai has its own service centre and a foreign-investment filing process that is familiar with Hong Kong and offshore parents.

Banking

Shenzhen banks are used to technology companies and move faster than Beijing or Shanghai, but they are also alert to cross-border e-commerce flows. Expect questions about payment channels, marketplace settlements and the relationship between the Chinese entity and the offshore seller.

Work permits

Shenzhen issues work permits through the municipal science and technology bureau and is comparatively fast for Category B. The city also has a well-used pathway for Hong Kong and Macau residents under the Greater Bay Area rules, which do not apply to other foreign nationals.

Address supply

¥6k–22k / year. Expect a lease, a property certificate and a utility bill in the company's name before a bank will look at the file.

Know before you commit

Three risks in this city

  • Hiring engineers on verbal offers: Shenzhen's labour tribunals enforce written contracts and severance strictly.
  • Treating a supplier's sample as a design handover without an NDA and an IP assignment.
  • Using a Qianhai entity for domestic sales without checking that the licence covers them.
